- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use moving average of last 5 days for smoothing.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.1 to 0.9 in 3–5 days), model exhibits lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and align with sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.
- In low-volatility periods (sentiment stable, price range <2%), model tends to drift toward mean; apply mean reversion rule: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×current sentiment-weighted average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 2–5% in early days; apply “early bias correction” by adding 1–2% to first 5 forecast points if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
